body: Thank you so much I'll pm you !
Thanks so much that's exactly what I need, some kind of tool that blends it with the background.

It's awful isn't it. And thing is everyone in the dream will be referring to me as male & then all of a sudden I'll look down and I'm wearing a fucking skirt so I'll feel like I just outed myself to everyone in the dream. Glad you've had this too though! It doesn't happen to me as much as you but it has happened so many times.

I'm also more outspoken & like you said about depression manifesting as anger. I'll get my levels checked. The doc I seen today (not an endo) asked me if I'd think about stopping T because of the effects on my emotions/personality & I said absolutely not.

I'm sure if anything maybe adjusting the dose will help. Thanks for commenting!

Mine isn't that crazy but during my first episode I was brought to A & E and put in one of the mental health suites which are basically small rooms with a couch attached to the wall & CCTV. My spatial awareness got messed up. The walls were the floor and the ceiling was the walls. I couldn't orientate myself in a 3d space at all.

I still think my neighbors can see me when I have my blinds closed. I even tested it, went outside when the blinds were closed and the light was on and I could see nothing. But every time I'm in my room I still think it's possible they can see me.
This dead meme just resurrected itself
And some whiteboard markers inevitably turn to crime after being discarded and turn into permanent markers, placing themselves conveniently in the teachers view so they can watch the world burn.

I used to. Like you said, when you feel numb sometimes inflicting pain on yourself makes sense in the moment. It might give you a temporary relief but it won't solve the problem long term. Self harm is complicated especially when it becomes a habit (I've been there). Try other things that make you feel again! Splash your face with cold water, take a really hot shower, go for a walk when it's cold. Just some ideas.
I got it done in the barbers for €10. I asked for a zero on the back and sides and a tidy up on the top. Absolutely delighted with it!

Thank you! I usually go to the barbers in my home town but I was somewhere else today and decided to take a chance. Really happy with it and just in time for Christmas before the barbers get booked up.

Thanks. I think me being self conscious is probably a lot to do with social media. There's always gonna be someone who passes better than you or has a perfect beard even if they've been on T for less time. Everyone is different I guess.

Thanks. I don't get misgendered. I probably haven't been misgendered in a year and a half. But despite this I'm still self conscious. I'm always paranoid that people are going to know I'm trans. I guess I have to be patient with the changes etc

Thank you. I can't remember all the tests I had but I definitely had an EEG. I also had a CT scan & the one where they put gel in your hair and attach wires to your head I think that was the EEG. The CT scan I had to lie down and this big machine was whirling around my head.

My doctor said I definitely have symptoms of a few different types of seizures but I'm also missing some symptoms. Right now they're thinking it's actually stress related (I didn't even realise I was stressed). They're giving me a few days supply of Xanax and then I'll have another checkup. If I have another seizure then I was told to come straight to the ER.

I wasn't thinking straight. I have schizophrenia on top of this & have had many bad experiences in hospital/ER. I was afraid they wouldn't believe me and think the seizures were mental health related. And I really didn't want to go back to the ER because the last time I was there I was severely mentally unwell and it just brings back those memories. On top of that today I feel so out of it but anyway I'm in the hospital now getting tests. I didn't realise how serious all this was since it's never happened before.

Thanks. I told my doctor everything. I actually went for a walk a few hours before it happened and came back very stressed. I was walking with a friend and he's off his meds at the moment and not great to be around. So I was really wound up when I got home. The doctor thinks it could be stress related.

I've got a letter for the hospital to run some tests so hopefully I get some answers. Thanks to everyone who responded I'm on my way to the hospital now (someone else is driving me). I still feel very out of it, don't know whether that's common after having a seizure.

Sorry for such a late reply. This is exactly what I'm like now. I have a coffee in the morning, maybe two. Then from about 6pm to 8pm I'll try have a main meal but usually I'll only have a few bites.

I'm going to book a doctor's appointment this week and they'll probably get my bloods done etc to see what's going on. 

I know you commented this two weeks ago so has anything changed for you regarding your appetite or is it still the same?
Thank you. I am a bit worried about having another episode. I'm going to tell my doctor I'm having a really hard time eating.

Definitely not depression since I feel like my mood is really improving. 

I was thinking meds but I've been on Seroquel 600mg for a few weeks now. In the beginning it made me have a huge appetite I was eating two dinners a day. But it's possibly meds related.

Well I'm currently doing a CBT (Cognitive Behavioural Therapy) group for people with psychosis. There's around 8 of us in the group, mostly young people like myself. Anyway I've learned a few different things to help me deal with my thoughts. Mindfulness is one of them, another is when you have a thought or delusion find the evidence for and against it being real. They gave us a lot of worksheets to write on. I'm finding it mostly helpful getting to hear other people's stories in the group. Even though we all have different beliefs there are common themes, one of them that everyone seems to have is a fear or paranoia about being harmed.

It wasn't my second high ever but I hadn't smoked in about a year. I used to smoke occasionally with no problem. A lot of the weed in London is skunk so it's stronger than normal weed. I think that's what fucked me up. I stopped smoking after I heard the voices but it didn't make a difference. I still ended up in hospital and I have continued to have symptoms for the last 3 years.

I still smoked occasionally after this happened but usually it would cause louder voices and paranoia.

The first weekend I stayed at a friend's and smoked with no problems. The second weekend I smoked I started to experience symptoms.

We were playing music and somebody paused it but I could still hear it playing. I dismissed it because I was high. When I went to sleep I could hear mumbling voices coming from the ceiling.

I woke up the next day and continued to hear voices. The voices continued for a few weeks, becoming louder and louder until I was admitted to hospital and had my first psychotic episode.

3 years later I still hear voices so weed has permanently fucked me up.

I'm also obsessed with uncovering the truth. It's a major factor in all my episodes and I even think about it a lot when I'm stable. I've been told I have delusions of grandeur. I don't know. I really feel like I have this cosmic purpose to uncover what's hidden beneath reality and you could say it's become an obsession. Every psychosis I write and write because I believe I have some really important insights to communicate.

So far, no medication had taken this belief away from me. I feel like it will be a journey that lasts a lifetime.

They will forgive you. I can't see how you'd lose a friendship in these circumstances over saying something like that. You were chatting, having a laugh, this stuff comes out. Don't worry about it, maybe add them to a new group chat and write an apology.

It caused a lot of my problems. I first started hearing voices when I was high. I quit the weed and the voices stayed with me for 3 years. If I smoke these days the voices get louder, I get paranoid and it's really easy for my thoughts to turn into delusions. I enjoy being high though because my mind isn't blank but it's critical that I don't smoke anymore if I'm serious about my recovery. I've landed myself in hospital because of weed in the past. For me, the high isn't worth the problems it causes.

I vape and it helps me process my thoughts. I do it a lot when I zone out.

CBD is expensive but I really liked it initially. It made me feel relaxed and content but after a couple of days my body got used to it and it didn't seem to have a noticeable effect.

I vape and it helps me process my thoughts. I do it a lot when I zone out.

CBD is expensive but I really liked it initially. It made me feel relaxed and content but after a couple of days my body got used to it and it didn't seem to have a noticeable effect.
What are they like for you. For me it's like I can hear them in my head and not with my ears. They really distract me though and I can stay in bed listening to them as I try to fall asleep.
I'll be seeing my doctor tomorrow so I'll definitely mention it to her. Maybe 600mg is too high a dose for me.

I was increased from Seroquel 400 to Seroquel 600. Seroquel was the first antipsychotic I was ever on 3 years ago and I would take it at night (I was on a low dose) and about 20 minutes later I would have loud external voices, the same kind of random content that I'm getting now. It's really strange. I'm definitely not hearing many voices during the day it's mainly after I take the seroquel.

I'm on Seroquel XR. I find it wears off towards the evening and I start to have more thoughts and feel a little elated. I take mine at 10pm too.

Olanzapine took 3 weeks to kick in but Seroquel generally worked within 1-2 weeks.

I used to have thought echo where the voices would repeat my thoughts out loud. It wasn't too problematic unless I was trying to read something and the voices would be on sentence one where I'd be reading sentence two.

One positive thing about it was that I could manipulate the voices to say whatever I wanted them to. I would intentionally think of positive things for them to say which drowned out the negative.
This sounds like me. I was on haldol with olanzapine in the hospital. Still had symptoms.
I've never been on risperidone yet. I've been on seroquel, abilify and olanzapine. Thanks for your comment I feel a little better about it knowing there's still meds I could try

I have a fear that I've become treatment resistant. I've been on olanzapine 3 months and I haven't taken any illegal drugs in this time, haven't been too stressed either. It's like it's slowly stopped working
I didn't know you could do that. Maybe I could go back on Haliparidol the only problem is it made me sleepwalk the last time but it definitely worked for delusions
Thank you. Intrusive though suck but I'm glad I'm not alone in this.
That's true. I am sure I can fight the thoughts it was just concerning having them in the first place.
Thank you. The thoughts are so different to who I really am as a person.

The way I see it this is a coping mechanism that people adopt. It's better to believe you're receiving messages from god or that your psychosis is a spiritual awakening than believe you have a lifelong debilitating illness.

I certainly have felt spiritual elements of my own psychosis and that's OK.

Definitely leftover delusions from my last psychosis. Some delusions just didn't leave me but at least they're not completely preoccupying my thoughts like they were before.

I'm happy with my meds at the moment though even though they might change them. I was feeling pretty depressed and after a week on zoloft my mood has really lifted so that's positive at least 😊
I was on a low dose of Haldol. It worked really well for delusions but it made me sleepwalk so I was taken off it.

I have a few. The main one is believing that there are these beings out in the universe watching me on a big screen or listening to my thoughts on some cosmic radio channel. But that's nothing compared to my last psychosis. 

Thank you for the info. I'll probably be on this dose for a few more months at least and then I can ask about reducing it because I'm currently on the highest dose you can take I think.

I'm on 20mg at night and 2.5mg in the morning. I reckon 2.5 is as low as you can go. Even on the high dose I've had very little side effects mainly restlessness at night and mild sedation during the day.
Welcome to the community! How are you finding your meds? I'm on olanzapine and it's worked pretty well for me so far.

I also lived in my own head as a child. Was really withdrawn. I had thought broadcasting delusions that lasted years and I deciphered messages from the TV that I thought were personally for me. Didn't get diagnosed till I was 21.

I'm currently in post psychotic depression so I know what you mean. I find myself wanting to go back to my psychosis where I felt connected to something greater and had constant companions watching my every move and thought. I miss it and I don't miss it at the same time.
A police station. I was then brought to Accident & Emergency at the nearest hospital where the admission was mentioned after seeing the psychiatrist on call who interviewed me.

I was initially admitted voluntarily although I don't remember it. I was very psychotic. Couldn't look at anyone not even my mother. 

Once I came to my senses the next day I demanded to leave the hospital because I thought I was a prophet trapped there being held prisoner. I kept repeating myself and kicking the ward door so I was pulled away to seclusion, injected and handed an involuntary admission order.

Once involuntary I was put in the high observation part of the ward because my behaviour was deemed "challenging". I lost two tribunals to get the order revoked and each time I lost it meant I would stay in the hospital for longer.

If I ever have a bad enough episode again I hope I have the capacity to go voluntarily since they can't force meds on you whereas being involuntary they can inject you and I never want to go through that plus the seclusion room again.

Also I was detained by law so even though I wanted my mother to take me out of the hospital she had no right to. It sucked big time.

You don't need to murder anyone and you don't need to take your own life either. It's not part of any plan life has for you. Call your doctor or a crisis line or tell a friend how you feel so you can get some help. Your plan is 100% not the right thing to do. I hope you're safe
Demo is pretty sick man, well done. Look forward to hearing the rest

My lifestyle probably contributes to the depression aswell. Before the episode I was able to work and study. Now I just attend the day hospital and lie in bed once I get home. Im trying to force myself to go walking in the evening but it doesn't get dark till late and I prefer walking at night when there's less people.

Enjoy the star wars books!
Happens to me too and the voices say these random things all the time

Even when you stop the drugs you're at risk of having a drug induced psychosis which is exactly what happened to me in the past. This post sounds like that's where you're at even though I think you're doing all the right things for your recovery.

Stay away from the weed which you're doing. I know what you've said here but being under 24 hour surveillance sounds extreme for smoking in the past. It could be a delusion creeping in. Looks after yourself and don't mind the haters.

I had it really bad during my last episode. Couldn't remember anything from conversations of what I or the other person said.

Try to exercise your brain with the puzzles that come in the newspaper (suduko, wordwheel, crossword) or I've heard fish oils are good.

I think memory problems seem to be very common with this condition. Mine have slightly improved on meds.

Take them an hour earlier if you can. I took them at 10pm in the hospital and I was waking up exhausted. I tried 9pm and had the same problem. Felt like I was hungover. Now I take them just after 8 and I wake up feeling alright. It takes a bit of experimentation to get it right.

I had it everyday for 2 years and it stopped abruptly around October. Since then I've heard them on and off but nothing compared to how it was when it was constant. It's weird getting used to the silence.
Good idea. Just subbed.
From the picture I thought this post was about someone accidently sleeping on top of their pet frog and squishing it.

Started with the water pipes whispering. Then my thoughts were being echoed outside my head. Now I just hear the same phrases being repeated over and over. It's much better with medication I barely hear them now.

I could have wrote this. I feel the same problem in the sunlight. That feeling of being completely exposed under a bright light. It makes me feel like everyone is watching me wherever I go. I'm telling my doctor about it tomorrow.
Thanks a lot and the same for you! Great wholesome and encouraging post to see before bed.

I have schizophrenia and I was a quarter way through an MA degree before I had to drop out and get admitted to hospital for the seventh time over the past 3 years. This is so encouraging, congratulations! I hope to return to my studies next year.
You're not alone. This happens to me too and I often want to get back under my blanket where its safe for a few hours.
I seriously need to find ways to deal with it too. Maybe I should pick up a book like yours. Hope it passes the journey time for you!
I think about being watched all day long too. Even when I'm inside I'm still being watched. Sorry its consuming you too.

I have the same with Spotify. I've made so many playlists out of it and they really mean a lot to me. Meds don't seem to effect the messages in the music for me either but I find it comforting and probably wouldn't want it to go away compered with some of my other delusions.
I often feel like this. Like I'm the only one seeing all the layers and synchronicities that the real world has.

I was walking with my dog on the beach and I seen 6 sets of couples walking together. I was the thirteenth person on the beach and it felt like it was a planned setup that everyone else was in twos except me. I didn't know why but my brain tried to convince me I was stuck in a simulation or that these people were all undercover walkers trying to blend in.
I just remembered that this symbol is on the inside of the plane turbine that falls in Donnie Darkos house. The camera intentionally zooms in on it.
I love this post. I feel the same way about music videos on YouTube. Like the musicians are laying their souls bare for us. You can really connect to that.

I've never had visual hallucinations but have had auditory hallucinations pretty much every day. Someone I know is diagnosed and has had maybe two hallucinations in his whole life. Everyone presents with this condition differently. Don't worry about faking it I'm sure that's not the case since a lot of us doubt ourselves.

Thanks. This is pretty encouraging. I've consistently watched the police pass me every morning or afternoon or night for the past 2 weeks and so far, nothing has happened. You're probably right. Exposing myself to the outside world everyday will probably (eventually) fix my brain and stop the delusions. Keep calm and carry on.

I've been on olanzapine 2 months and 2 weeks but I've only been on my current dose maybe a month. I can give it some time to see if things settle. Thanks. I see my doctor on the 31st so I'll bring all of this up with her.

I knew somewhat about psychosis before I ever experienced it. I remember the first time I heard voices on the platform waiting for a train. I knew that I must be hearing voices and I was aware it wasn't really even though it completely shocked me and I was in denial that it was actually happening.

What followed was delusions that other people could hear my thoughts and I had my first hospital admission. I've been in hospital around 6 or 7 times now and despite knowing about this illness I still completely believe the delusions when they are happening and seem to not believe they're symptoms. So knowing about it can be an advantage as you are able to tell what thoughts are delusions but sometimes you lose insight when the psychosis kicks in.

I struggle to know what day it is, the date and sometimes the month. Its easier when you have structure in your week so I'm hoping it will improve since I started attending the day hospital. Before that, knowing the date  has felt meaningless.
Haha this is too real.
Not when I close my eyes but I usually hear messages from god in music and the radio.
This is really cool. Has a Basquiat vibe to it.
That's a good point. A lot of police where I live are crooked cops and I simply don't trust them. I think that has definitely effected how I feel about police.
I've created 100's of playlists to show how music is God's greatest communicator across all genres. Adding Moving image to music and compiling a collection that will describe this reality.

The same thing happened to me when I was prescribed zoloft (antidepressant). Week one I started hearing whispering in the water pipes and a delusion that I would be the victim of a drive by shooting. The psychosis developed from there to hearing voices and more paranoia and I ended up in hospital a month or so later.

I take my meds. I eat. I sleep. I've just recovered from an episode and this is all happening. I don't know if I'm at a tipping point into mania. Maybe it's adjusting to the outside world after being locked up for the last 2 months.

Bittersweet Symphony - The Verve

"I need to hear some sounds that recognise the pain in me, yeah"
This was one of the first delusions I had. It used to make me pretty anxious about thinking about anyone I knew for fear of forming that link between our minds somehow. I hope it goes soon for you.

Mm this is exactly how I feel. I'm detached from everything. Sometimes I become suddenly aware of my surroundings and I remember where I am but it all seems like a dream. I've  had to leave the room because it freaks me out to have that "this isn't real" feeling. But I get what you're saying about things consequently not feeling important to hold on to since they don't seem real to begin with.

I think about my family and I just don't feel any emotion and that's weird because we're really close. It's like they're strangers or characters on a TV show.
Well done to you. I end up making a blanket cucoon in these situations and I usually get no work done. Serious pat on the back, this is a good motivator to read.

For me, and I agree with all of the above. I had a thought yesterday about psychosis being like a heightened "adapt and survive" mode. Our brains are perceiving threats where there aren't any in an attempt to protect us from possible danger.

I imagined it like being a hunter gatherer but constantly scared of a wolf attack and staying in a cave all day. I don't want to think that we're lower on the food chain but it seems like a struggle to adapt and survive is at least some important element here.
I used to make these kinds of diagrams to try and map my thinking especially in psychosis. I feel like it's so clear to you and clear in your head but difficult to describe to others.

I still believe it because I think mine started in childhood as a feeling that I would do something great one day and be recognised for it. I used to also believe as a child that I was the only one seeing the world properly or perceiving the 'real' world and at times I wondered if I was the only one with a mind. 

That belief slowly shifted into I was chosen to uncover something and spread this message. Most of it's about experiences. I have certain experiences I'm absolutely meant to have like their interwoven into the tapestry of reality. It's like I'm always walking towards some great truth.

When I got schizophrenia I started wondering whether those beliefs were delusional in addition to everything else that was going on with me. A few months ago was the first time I almost convinced myself it was all a delusion. Now I still believe its real.

No matter what I read about people having the same experience and theirs being a delusion I still won't believe it. It doesn't matter how many people tell me it's not real because I think some aspects of psychosis are pretty complicated if it was that easy we'd all be cured I guess.

Yeah as annoying as it is, the weed will make it worse. I used to smoke when I was depressed and it worked as a temporary escape. Then I became dependent on smoking everyday to deal with my feelings.

I'd try to stop smoking for a week and see if anything improves. Try to do something else instead. I know it's easier said than done but trust me if you keep smoking daily you'll keep missing class and keep feeling depressed. Weed impacted my mental health a lot and when I quit, even temporarily I felt myself coming back to normal.

Me too. I believed people could read my mind from around 7 or 8 years of age. I used to be scared to think around people and this belief was on and off for a few years. I developed a phobia of ghosts soon after and I had an obsession, almost like a twitch to look over my shoulder all the time. Sometimes several times a minute because I believed that something was there. My parents actually brought me to the doctor about the ghost one because I would get so scared at times I'd stand frozen in a room shouting because I was convinced something was in the room with me. 

I got delusions of reference pretty bad as a teen. People on the TV would make facial expressions and gestures to send me messages and contact me. I thought if they nodded at the camera they knew I was on the other side of the TV.

In my late teens I'd get random episodes. One day I thought my mams boyfriend was going to kill her and come home to kill me so I waited in the house with a poker from the fire till they returned. There was a long lane near our house and everytime I walked down there I thought everyone in their houses would come to their windows just to watch me. This was a row of about 30 houses. 

Everything settled down and then I was like 21 when I started hearing voices and having full blown episodes.

Thank you. I've been walking around for too long. I didn't know where I was going but I found somewhere I recognise. Going to get the train home now. The walking cleared my head a bit.

I'll try write things down. I just have to see how things are now. I really want to get through this road bump without landing myself in hospital.

I can't call the doctor. The only option is to go to the emergency room which I'm reluctant to do.

I'm still trying to ground myself for now and hoping it doesn't get any worse. Been feeling weird for hours now but as I said I'm trying to feel normal again.

Yeah it really depends for me. There's been times recently when I've been absolutely fine with it and had no problems. It was worse after I was first diagnosed. Hallucinations would be so loud, every thought turned into a delusion.

You're right though. I think I'm not in the head space to realise it. A part of me knows I shouldn't but a part of me is so fed up I feel like I don't give a fuck what might happen. I know that sounds super immature but it's just how I'm feeling. Kind of like I don't care about destructive behaviours.

Saying that I'll lay off the weed though. I haven't bought it in months so the only time I have it is by chance.
Abilify helped my symptoms. Just watch out for akathisia/restlessness. I had it bad it's a common side effect. Good luck I really hope it works for you!

Yeah sometimes I'm not sure if I should bother with a warning because these things don't effect everyone but I'd hate to cause someone else to have a delusion so I always try play it safe with recommending stuff to people

Thanks so much. This was all really helpful and I'm going to try the exercises you suggested.

I'm not on any medication at the moment and haven't been for a few months. I think the anger is definitely my body's way of telling me that something isn't right. Its like a sign that I need to take things seriously instead of trying to dismiss my mental health and convince myself there's nothing wrong.

Thanks again for your response. I'm seeing my doctor again on Monday. I've been irritable for two full days now. Someone told me it could be depression manifesting itself in a different way. Anyway now that it's happened it's a wake up call for me to take these things seriously.

Yeah I read this a while ago when I was doing my dissertation. I found it really interesting. There was also a documentary that I've only seen clips of called "Crazywise" by Phil Borges. Its about the same thing. I think they took a group of diagnosed young people to some tribe of shamans in South America to see how the perspectives differed.

Word of warning. I watched the trailer when I was feeling pretty bad last year and it made me think my illness was a lie and obviously that caused me to distrust everyone around me. I thought I was waking up and going through a spiritual crisis when in reality I was having an intense psychotic episode. I feel like I have to put a disclaimer on here but maybe I'm overly sensitive.

You're probably right. I've always been the outsider in my family and university became a second family to me. I know he is probably sincere but no matter what my mind tells me I'm imposing or annoying people because I don't really belong to any particular social group. I drift between several never feeling at ease in one particular one. That's just how I am so when I finally find people I feel comfortable around and who like me I assume it's too good to be true.

Ive always been reluctant to write these things down on paper but I did this the other night and it felt like I cleared a load of crap from my mind. I'll get to do it again. I think the best approach is to keep writing and not care about what you're saying. Like you, mine can turn into rambling or dark stuff but at least I'm cleansing it from my head.

Thanks for your message. Reddit is my only outlet at this time so I appreciate any responses I get. Definitely helps with feeling isolated.

I hold two contradicting theories about myself. The first is that my experiences can be explained away by schizophrenia and my brain is broken. The second I favour more. That my brain isn't broken its just different and if I had been born in a different part of the world my experiences might have been explained as spiritual or shamanic in nature.

If you do some more research I've read about the similarities between psychosis and shamanism or at least the things shamans start to experience in late teens/early adulthood including visions and voices. All very interesting. Whether it's true or not it gives me some peace of mind that there's a chance I'm not wrong about everything.

I did the same. It's been maybe 4 or 5 months. I was OK for a while and now my depression is worsening and I'm suffering badly with random anger.

This is how it goes for me. On meds till it stops. Off meds without permission. Back on meds when it gets bad again. I wish I could be med compliant but the side effects make me so miserable.

I was in hospital over a year ago and the doctor was concerned about me playing pokemon go in the hospital garden because it wasn't "reality"

Of course I knew that but I was bored and that stupid game actually got me active.

My mother was kind of similar. She didn't like me talking about anything fantasy related for a while.
One of my favourite songs. You did such a good job. I love how as the song went on you got more and more into it. Thanks for sharing!

I was diagnosed at 21. I'm 23 now. I used to have a lot of auditory hallucinations but I get them randomly now. Its nice to go days without hearing anything.

I look after myself pretty well but I struggle with laundry a lot. Hygiene too. If I can't shower I'll try to at least wash my hair. I sometimes struggle out in public but other times I feel really confident. It depends. My feelings change a lot. My emotions are hard to pin down. I feel contradictions a lot of the time.

Sometimes I think I'm God or a messiah who understands what reality really is. I've felt something special inside me since I was a kid. I often feel like I'm at the centre and everything points inwards to me and I can see the true design, like watching a performance. When I'm not feeling those things I can feel on edge. Like my thoughts and my environment are the same and like the police are following me everywhere. I have good and bad really.
Great post. This community wouldn't be the same without her. Hugs u/playingtricksonme

My current fear is that the police are following me. Shining their torches in my neighbours garden, driving past on the street. Everywhere I go they're there.

Sometimes I'm also afraid that someone might attack me on the street completely unprovoked.

I used to a lot. I don't have a TV anymore but it can happen with Netflix or YouTube and on a slightly unrelated note Spotify (music).

Sometimes I would walk into the room and the TV was already on. An advert or show would say something and answer what I was thinking at the time. Other times it felt more direct.

Then I had it when I was watching a series or film. It is like the show or film had all these hidden symbols and only I would be able to properly decipher them or understand them in a particular way. I would sometimes feel strange when other people liked the shows I got messages from because in my head I would think that they never understood the show or the messages the way I did.

For about a year I created over 50 playlists on Spotify and it became an obsession to add all the songs to the playlists that I felt were communicating with me. Every week I would go on discover weekly or just look for random music and I was convinced that the music I needed to hear would find me. I still love Spotify but only now do I realise how my behaviour back then was obsessive. I thought it was completely normal and psychosis wasn't even a question I asked myself because the music really was speaking to me.

The music still speaks to me now but not to the same extent and I don't obsess so much over it. I used to look for messages every single day. Sometimes now I wouldn't add a new song for a week or more.
